Yet the region still had a substantial military force to maintain.
一些重要迹象表明，帝国得以重新安排君士坦丁堡的粮食供应，并调整为部分行省军队提供谷物的产地。前面已经简略指出，从帕夫拉戈尼亚与本都一些地方的花粉数据来看，与罗马晚期传统农业有关的一整套作物，在一些范围有限的地区持续种植到八世纪。到了七世纪中叶之后，生产又更侧重于谷物和畜牧。虽然证据并不明确，仍可看出，与南面更易受袭的地区相比，这些地方谷物生产所占的比重可能有所上升。

There are some significant indications that the empire had been able to reorient its management of both the Constantinopolitan supply as well as the centers of grain production for some of its provincial armies. We have already noted briefly that the palynological data for parts of Paphlagonia and Pontus suggest not only that the suite of crops associated with traditional late Roman agriculture continued to be cultivated in some limited areas into the eighth century but also that production after the middle of the seventh century placed increased emphasis on cereals and the herding of livestock. While the evidence is ambiguous, it is possible to see a proportional increase of cereal production in these areas compared with more exposed regions to the south.
安纳托利亚各地农业产出趋于简化，尤其是花粉数据所显示的更偏重谷物生产，事实上对当时面临巨大压力的东罗马国家来说，来得非常及时。六至八世纪间，安纳托利亚北部、西北部和中部经历了一段气候比以前更湿润的时期，至少持续到730年代，这很可能也促进了谷物生产。中世纪作家，例如十一世纪的米海尔·普塞洛斯，以及有学问的拜占庭人所读的罗马农学文献，都强调有规律的冬春季降雨（十一月至次年四月）对谷物种植的重要性。
从既有格局转向较简单的谷物与畜牧生产，有几个地方显然在五世纪起就已发生，但代用数据表明，多数地方是在七至八世纪完成转变的。无论这个过程是否由地方条件促成、各地速度是否不同，自650年代起政府陷入的困境，一定加重了国库筹措各军队所需物资的压力。军队需要的正是牲畜和谷物，也就是花粉记录显示日益占主导地位的两类产品。

Such a simplification of agrarian output across Anatolia, and more especially the greater emphasis on cereal production suggested by the palynological data, would in fact have been very opportune for the east Roman state under the sort of intense pressure that it experienced at this time. The fact that northern, northwestern, and central Anatolia experienced a period of greater humidity from the sixth into the eighth century— lasting at least into the 730s— than had hitherto been the case may well have acted to encourage cereal production also. The importance for cereal farming of the regular winter and spring rainfall (November to April) was emphasized by medieval writers such as Michael Psellus (in the eleventh century) as well as in the Roman agronomical literature that learned Byzantines read.

Although it is clear that the change from the established pattern to the simpler grain and livestock regime was under way in a few places from the fifth century onward, the proxy data suggest that in most cases the shift took place in the seventh to eighth centuries. Whether or not this process was the result of local conditions and evolved at different rates in different regions, the desperate straits in which the government found itself from the 650s on must certainly have constituted a further pressure on the fisc to generate the supplies needed by its armies— livestock and grain, precisely the products that the pollen record suggests came to dominate.
葡萄和橄榄等面向市场的作物，在东地中海的文化背景下仍属“必需品”。如花粉证据所示，这些作物仍有人生产，不过规模已大大缩小。如前所述，七世纪后期在君士坦丁堡附近引入橄榄栽培，很可能反映了大约同期锡诺普地区这一产业的显著衰落。米利都地区的证据也支持这种说法。
这究竟反映了市场需求萎缩，还是经济或气候因素造成的生产崩溃，抑或上述因素共同作用，仍不得而知。

Market-orientated produce such as vines and olives, still “essentials” in an eastern Mediterranean cultural context, continued to be produced but on a much-reduced scale, as the pollen evidence appears to indicate. And as I noted earlier, the introduction of oleoculture close to Constantinople during the later seventh century may well reflect the apparent collapse of the Sinope region industry at roughly the same time. The evidence from the Miletus region would support such an argument.
Whether this reflects a shrunken market demand, a breakdown in production due to economic or climatic factors, or a combination of all of these still remains obscure.
政府把军事供应及关键给养，尤其谷物和肉类的生产看得极为重要。最后一个迹象，就是军队从原先驻地撤出之后，在安纳托利亚如何安置。在这个过程中，一个重要特点是，各支部队似乎分驻在各个行省，所选地区与当地供养他们的能力相称。这一点本该显而易见，却多年来一直无人留意。撤军的确切用意当然仍不清楚，但结果相当明显。

例如，亚美尼亚野战军约一万二千至一万五千人，分驻于广阔的地域。这里在战略上不易受攻击，多是山地和难以居住的地形，从阿拉伯人的主要前沿基地较难到达，农业潜力也有限。相反，从叙利亚和美索不达米亚的东部边境撤出的一支名义上人数较多的部队，分驻在面积较小、产出却更丰厚的地区，那里在战略上当然也更易受袭。下一章会讨论这一点。这里要说的是，政府显然有一套周密计划来驻扎、供应与维持军队，也有计划继续为都城供应谷物，并且想必也为士兵供应谷物。这些问题也将在下一章谈到。

A final indication of the centrality for the government of issues of military supply and the production of key provisions— grain and meat in particular—is the way in which the armies were accommodated in Anatolia after their withdrawal from the regions in which they had originally been based. It is a significant feature of this process that the different divisions appear to have been billeted or based across provinces according to the ability of the districts to support them. This ought to be obvious, yet for many years it simply was not noticed. Of course, the exact rationale underlying the withdrawal remains obscure, but the outcome is clear enough.

Thus, a force of some 12,000–15,000 from the field army of Armenia was garrisoned across a vast swathe of territory but in a landscape that was both less strategically vulnerable, consisting largely of mountain and inhospitable terrain relatively difficult of access from the major Arab forward bases and with only limited agricultural potential; whereas a nominally larger force withdrawn from the eastern frontier in Syria and Mesopotamia was located in a smaller but more productive and certainly strategically more vulnerable landscape. I will deal with this in the next chapter. Suffice to say that the government clearly had a plan, and a sophisticated one, for the garrisoning, supplying, and maintaining of its armies, and it also had a plan for the continuation of grain supplies for the capital as well as, we may assume, for the soldiers. I will deal with these aspects also in the following chapter.

对东罗马国家而言，那是一段艰难的时期。尽管史料稀少，许多又含义不明，我们仍能窥见帝国得以存续的基础。这一时期气候多变且不稳定，似乎对小亚细亚乃至更远地区的农业生产与耕作产生了显著、甚至足以使之转型的影响。人口减少，用于生产的土地面积缩小，许多地方的农业体系大为简化。与此同时，城市生活和城乡关系也在重新塑造。对波斯的战争，尤其是640年代以后对阿拉伯人的战争，也迫使政府彻底重新思考如何供养军队、向君士坦丁堡供应物资，以及保卫核心领土，这些问题将在后文讨论。如前所述，也如下一章将看到的，从北非或西西里运到都城的粮食有时仍很重要。西西里与意大利南部的代用气候数据表明，公元450—750年间该地区经历的湿润气候，很有利于集约种植谷物。

然而，安纳托利亚继续生产维持生存所必需的物产。事实上，如果花粉数据准确反映了当时情形，安纳托利亚的农业总产出虽在下降，谷物生产所占比例却似有所增长。这种比重的上升，可视为弥补了帝国谷物来源的衰减或丧失，也弥补了水果、橄榄和葡萄栽培等其他生产活动的衰退或消失。牲畜饲养似乎也同样在农业经济中变得更为突出。在人口显著减少、领土急剧萎缩的背景下，这或许已经足以满足政府与行省生产人口的需要。把这些情况同下一章将讨论的东罗马政府的组织方式结合起来，就能够逐步看清这些变化，进而更全面地解释中世纪的东罗马帝国如何走出七世纪中叶陷入的危局。我希望，这样的解释是可信的。

These were hard times for the east Roman state. Yet in spite of the sparseness of the sources and the ambiguity of many of them, we can glimpse the basis for its survival. Shifting and unstable climatic conditions in this period seem to have had a significant— indeed, transformative— impact on agricultural production and farming across Asia Minor and beyond. Population declined, the amount of land productively exploited receded, the agrarian regime was in many places considerably simplified, and all this in the context of a reshaping of urban life and a refashioning of urban– rural relations. In the context of the wars with the Persians but much more dramatically with the Arabs after the 640s, the government had also to completely rethink the ways in which it supported its armies, supplied Constantinople, and defended its core territories, issues that I will address later. Imports to the capital from North Africa or Sicily remained important at times, as we have noted and as we will see in the next chapter— and the proxy climate data from Sicily and southern Italy show that the humid climate that this region experienced in the period 450–750 CE was highly favorable for the intensive production of cereals.

Nevertheless, Anatolia continued to produce the essentials for survival. In fact, if the palynological data reflect the situation accurately, the production of grain in Anatolia appears to make up an increasing proportion of a declining total agricultural output, a proportional increase that could be seen to compensate for the decline or disappearance both of sources of grain no longer available and of other activities (fruticulture, oleoculture, and viticulture), while stockbreeding appears likewise to become a more prominent aspect of the agrarian economy. In the context of a marked demographic decline and a dramatic shrinkage of territory, this might have been enough to provide for the needs of the government and the provincial producing populations. When we combine this information with organizational aspects of east Roman government to be discussed in the next chapter, we can begin to see through the haze surrounding these developments to generate a more rounded and, I hope, plausible account of the way in which the medieval Eastern Roman Empire emerged from the crisis conditions into which it was plunged in the middle of the seventh century.
